transcript.text: I can help with that. To narrow it down quickly: is your Hoover a corded model or battery-powered? If it's corded, please check that the plug is firmly in the wall socket and that the fuse hasn't blown (if it's a UK 3-pin plug). If it's battery-powered, does it charge correctly when plugged into its charger?
its corded, the red Henry one. the plug is in and the socket works, my lamp works in it. there is some black tape on the wire near the plug

[Heading: Damaged power cord or loose connection]
The black tape near the plug is a significant clue; it often hides damage to the cable where it flexes most, which can cause an internal break and stop the vacuum from working. Please unplug the machine first for safety. Carefully inspect that taped area: if you see any cuts in the outer plastic coating or exposed copper wires, do not use it as this is a fire and shock hazard. Also check inside the plug to ensure the wires are tight and not loose. If the cable looks intact but it still won't start, we may need to look at internal components like the thermal cut-out.

the tape is a bit bent there, my son did it ages ago. i cant see any wires under it. it came on for a second once when i moved the wire then went off again, i wont do that again. i havent got a screwdriver for the plug

[Heading: Damaged power cord]
That behaviour—working for a second when you move the wire—is the classic sign of an internal break in the copper wires where they enter the plug. Because this is a mains-powered appliance and you don't have the tools to safely open the plug or re-terminate the cable, it is not safe for you to attempt a repair yourself. Please stop using the vacuum immediately; a broken wire can spark and cause a fire. You should take it to a local appliance repair shop or an electrician who can replace the plug end or the entire cable safely. If the machine is old, they may advise that replacement is more cost-effective than the repair.
